title: SIEM onboarding: field negotiation and retention proposal
content:
Purpose:
This note is a practical proposal and negotiable checklist for onboarding enterprise SIEM partners (Splunk/Datadog/Azure Sentinel). Focus: a minimal required export contract, optional fields, retention constraints, privacy-safe defaults, and a lightweight transformer architecture customers can run in their VPC/edge to meet regulatory constraints.

Background / motivation:
- We keep getting slightly different field requests from customers; engineering spends time creating one-off adapters.
- Need a repeatable negotiation playbook to reduce scope creep and speed onboarding.
- Combine security requirements (audit schema) with product constraints (throughput/backpressure, field cardinality, PII redaction).

Scope:
- Target integrators: Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, Azure Sentinel (CEF/Log Analytics).
- Payloads: audit events, export evidence pointers, RBAC-change events, and operational telemetry (export delivery status).
- Not in scope: deep transformation of customer log schemas unrelated to audit/evidence (those are out-of-band).

High-level requirements (negotiable):
1) Minimal required fields (these must be present in every event):
   - event_id (string)
   - timestamp_utc (ISO-8601 string)
   - event_type (string; e.g., "audit.login", "siem.export.delivery")
   - actor.principal (string; pseudonymized if requested)
   - resource.id (string)
   - outcome (string; success|failure|partial)
   - redaction_markers (list of strings, empty list if none)

2) Optional recommended fields (for richer analytics):
   - actor.ip
   - actor.user_agent
   - request.id (internal correlation id)
   - route.model (e.g., "gpt-4o-mini")
   - tokens.used (integer)
   - evidence.pointer (URI or internal id)

3) Retention and PII constraints (proposal for negotiation):
   - Default: customer chooses retention in their SIEM. Redwood exposes a retention TTL header on exported events for customer-run connectors.
   - For hosted exports (Redwood-managed forwarder): default retention 90 days; for accounts requiring shorter retention, allow opt-down to 30 days with SLA caveats.
   - PII rule: by default redact direct PII (email, phone) from event body; design contract to allow customers to request raw fields via a signed retention/processing addendum (legal + security review).

4) Throughput and SLAs:
   - Typical export peak: 200 events/s for medium enterprise (reference: internal metric).
   - Throttling behavior: exporter should return HTTP 429 with Retry-After. Contract: Redwood will buffer up to X minutes (configurable), then drop with a clear metric.
   - Backpressure: recommend a 3-tier fallback: live export -> batched export to S3 -> on-demand pull.

Transformation/adapter architecture (recommendation):
- Two supported deployment topologies:
  A) Customer-managed lightweight transformer (preferred for privacy): runs in customer's VPC, receives Redwood-formatted events via TLS, performs PII redaction and final mapping, pushes to SIEM.
  B) Redwood-managed forwarder with per-customer redaction rules (used when customer requests managed service).

- Transformer responsibilities:
  - Validate minimal schema and enrich with correlation metadata.
  - Apply field allowlist/denylist (customer-configurable).
  - Apply pseudonymization/hashing for actor.principal when requested (salted HMAC with customer key).
  - Collapse high-cardinality fields (e.g., raw prompt text) into evidence pointers and store in secure artifact store.
  - Emit delivery status events back to Redwood (deliveries/failed attempts).

Sample minimal JSON schema (stringified for contract):
- audit_event_version: "1.2"
- payload: { event_id, timestamp_utc, event_type, actor_principal, resource_id, outcome, extras_json }
(note: extras_json should be a string-encoded JSON to avoid SIEM field explosion)

Mapping examples (quick) - please treat as examples, not exhaustive:  
- Splunk HEC (recommended): send event as JSON to /services/collector/event with index specified by customer. Use "sourcetype": "redwood:audit:1". Put core fields at root, large text fields under "extras" key.

- Datadog Logs: use attributes as top-level facets. Add tags: "redwood_customer:<customer-id>", "redwood_env:<env>". Set "dd.source": "redwood-audit". Keep prompt/evidence as URL in "extras.evidence_url".

- Azure Sentinel / Log Analytics: prefer CEF mapping when possible, otherwise ingest as custom JSON. Recommended mapping: CEF extension fields for outcome and resource_id, and a custom column set for extras_json.

Field negotiation playbook (practical steps):
1) Discovery call (CS + Customer Sec + Eng): capture required retention/pseudonymization/legal constraints. Use template questions below.
2) Share minimal contract (this doc as starting point) + proposed mapping example for customer's SIEM.
3) Customer reviews; mark fields as: required / optional / blocked. If blocked -> propose pointer replacement.
4) Security review if raw PII requested -> requires signed DPA addendum + KMS key exchange if pseudonymization only.
5) Test plan sign-off (see below).

Customer discovery template (short):
- SIEM vendor and ingestion method (HEC, API key, Log Collector)
- Desired retention (days) and regulatory constraints
- PII sensitivity level (low/medium/high) and acceptable pseudonymization approach
- Expected peak events/sec and average event size
- Preferred index/naming and tag schema
- SLA for delivery (acceptable data lag)

Testing and validation plan:
- Phase 0: Schema smoke test (10 sample events).
- Phase 1: Bulk delivery (10k events) into staging index, validate field mapping and cardinality impact.
- Phase 2: Failure injection (simulate 429s, network failure), validate buffering and retry behavior and verify Redwood delivery-status metrics.
- Acceptance: customer verifies queries for 5 common audit use-cases (login audit, RBAC-change, export evidence retrieval).

Operational metrics to publish to console for the customer: 
- daily_export_events_total
- export_delivery_success_rate (per SIEM endpoint)
- export_buffered_mb_last_24h
- export_dropped_events_total
- avg_export_latency_ms

Privacy & legal notes (must be explicit in negotiation):
- Avoid shipping raw user content (prompts/responses) by default. If customer requests content, route through evidence pointer and use secure artifact pull with signed short-lived URLs.
- For EU regulated customers: require transformer in-customer VPC unless DPA allows Redwood-managed processing.
- Logging of pseudonymization salt operations must be auditable (store logs with restricted access).

Sample onboarding checklist (quick):
- [ ] Internal kick-off meeting (CS, Sec, Eng)
- [ ] Customer fills discovery template
- [ ] Contract: agree retention and PII handling (legal)
- [ ] Decide deployment topology (A or B above)
- [ ] Provide SIEM ingest endpoints and credentials (customer)
- [ ] Run Phase 0 and Phase 1 tests
- [ ] Failover/backpressure test (Phase 2)
- [ ] Acceptance and move to prod

Common negotiation compromises we can offer quickly:
- Replace raw_principal with hashed_principal if customer needs identity analytics but not raw PII.
- Replace prompt_text with evidence.pointer + metadata (token_count, snippet_hash).
- Provide 30-day managed retention for new customers for first 90 days, then default to customer-managed retention.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- How many concurrent customer-managed transformer instances do we want to support in onboarding automation? (TBD: SRE input)
- Should we add a signed-s3-presigned-url pattern for evidence retrieval in every event by default? pros/cons: convenience vs accidental exposure. (ask legal)
- Decide exact HMAC algorithm & key rotation cadence for pseudonymization. (crypto team)

Next steps (owner assigned below):
- Asha: circulate to CS and Eng (by 2025-02-14) and request feedback on the sample schema.
- Luis: draft a lightweight transformer reference (container, 600MB image target) and post prototype PR to GitHub.
- Claire: draft the DPA addendum language for raw content processing options.
- Devon: run cost model for managed-forwarder vs customer-managed topology.

Notes to self / meeting snippets:
- customer X asked for full prompt retention -> route to evidence pointer + legal review.
- we should add telemetry tag for model-version to help debug quality regressions.

Appendix: example small event (single-line for SIEM)
{
  "event_id": "evt_20250207_abc123",
  "timestamp_utc": "2025-02-07T18:22:11Z",
  "event_type": "audit.export.delivery",
  "actor_principal": "hash:HMAC-SHA256:abcd...",
  "resource_id": "res_cloud_api_42",
  "outcome": "success",
  "extras_json": "{\"route.model\":\"gpt-4o-mini\",\"tokens_used\":123}"
}

If you have feedback, mark with inline comments here or add to JIRA-SIEM-1234.
